reply: We need a few key facts before picking a method – what you’re trying to measure, how the liquid looks optically, and any reference analysis you can run. Then a quick lab screening (e.g., NIR transmission and MIR‑ATR on the same sample set) will tell which spectral region captures the contaminant signatures.

concept.summary: Perform an initial laboratory feasibility study using two complementary in‑line‑compatible techniques on representative process samples: (1) NIR transmission (1–5 mm path) for bulk liquid absorption, and (2) MIR‑ATR (1–6 µm penetration) using a standard cuvette or ATR probe. Collect spectra while simultaneously measuring the reference value of the target variable. Build separate chemometric models (e.g., PLS regression) for each technique and compare performance.
concept.probe: NIR transmission probe (1–5 mm path) and MIR‑ATR probe (ATR crystal) in a lab cuvette holder
concept.location: Laboratory bench, using process samples drawn from the line
concept.fiberLink: Standard silica fiber for NIR; chalcogenide fiber for MIR‑ATR (as supported by AFS multimodal probes)
concept.analyzer: Bench‑top NIR spectrometer (≈[to be agreed with the customer]) and MIR FT‑IR spectrometer with ATR accessory

risks: If the liquid is highly scattering or opaque, NIR transmission may saturate and MIR‑ATR may suffer from limited penetration.
Chemometric models may overfit if the training set is too small or not representative of process variability.
Without a known target variable, model validation cannot be completed.

steps: Collect a set of process liquid samples covering normal operation and off‑spec events.
Measure each sample with NIR transmission and MIR‑ATR under identical conditions.
Obtain reference values for the suspected contaminant or quality variable using the existing lab method.
Develop separate calibration models for each technique and evaluate prediction error on a held‑out validation set.
Select the technique that meets the agreed‑upon prediction performance and practical constraints (probe cleaning, fiber length, cost).
feasibility.decisionBasis: Model performance (RMSEP, bias) compared against acceptance criteria agreed with the customer; cost and ease of integration also considered.
